records.title: Engineering the synovial lining-sublining architecture in a human 3D model to study macrophage-fibroblast interactions in arthritis.
records.abstract: The synovial membrane is a key regulator of joint homeostasis, inflammation, and tissue remodeling, yet human in vitro models that reproduce its spatial organization while enabling controlled investigation of macrophage-fibroblast-like stromal cell (FLS) interactions remain limited. Here, we developed a xeno-free, spatially organized 3D synovial membrane model that reconstructs the structural relationship between the macrophage lining and fibroblast-rich sublining compartment.The model was generated by establishing an apically organized macrophage-containing lining-like compartment on a transwell membrane, followed by stepwise assembly of FLS laden hydrogel constructs. Hydrogel screening identified a 1:3 VitroGel® RGD formulation as the most suitable condition to support FLS viability, homogeneous cell distribution, and stable tissue organization. Experimentally induced M1-like and M2-like macrophages were incorporated, and the model was stimulated with TNF-α, TGF-β, or OA synovial fluid (SF). Cytotoxicity, proliferation, metabolic activity, gene expression, and cytokine secretion were analyzed. Pharmacological responsiveness was evaluated using adalimumab and 4-octyl itaconate (4-OI).The spatially organized construct enabled compartment-specific analysis of macrophage-FLS communication. M1-like macrophages induced inflammatory FLS responses characterized by elevated IL1B, IL6, TNFA, and MMP1 expression, whereas M2-like macrophages promoted matrix-remodeling and myofibroblast-related programs, including increased TGFB and ACTA2 expression. Exposure to OA-SF and cytokine stimulation induced FLS hyperproliferation, metabolic adaptation, and distinct transcriptional responses. Treatment with adalimumab suppressed TNF-driven inflammatory responses, whereas 4-OI reduced selected inflammatory markers and altered remodeling-associated responses.Together, these findings establish a spatially organized, xeno-free 3D synovial membrane model as a defined and experimentally tractable platform for studying macrophage-FLS communication and synovial activation. By combining physiologically inspired tissue organization with compartment-specific analysis, the model provides a human in vitro platform for investigating OA-associated inflammatory and remodeling processes and evaluating pharmacological modulation under defined experimental conditions.

records.title: An innervated and vascularized HNSCC-on-a-chip model built on defined and tunable engineered extracellular matrices.
records.abstract: Understanding the tumor microenvironment requires experimental platforms that faithfully recapitulate its key components. Here, we present an innervated and vascularized head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC)-on-a-chip platform built with fully defined and tunable engineered extracellular matrices (eECMs). In a stepwise increase of complexity, we first cocultured patient-derived HNSCC cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts, and endothelial cells within tailored eECMs, revealing extracellular matrix-dependent differences in transcriptional state, multicellular self-organization, and chemotherapeutic sensitivity. We then integrated these three-dimensional constructs into a cancer-vasculature interface, which enabled analysis of eECM-dependent directional collective migration and invasion. Finally, we incorporated trigeminal innervation through injectable 3D human bioengineered trigeminal ganglia, establishing a chip-based innervation-tumor-vasculature tri-interface. Together, this all-human platform integrates fully defined ECM, vasculature, and innervation in a single modular system to investigate tumor organization, invasion, and therapeutic responses within a controlled human microenvironment.

records.title: Altered developmental trajectories in neurodevelopmental disorders: mechanisms, human models and translational perspectives.
records.abstract: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) are clinically and genetically heterogeneous conditions often studied through diagnostic categories, causal genes, synaptic dysfunction or end-stage phenotypes. Although these approaches remain essential, they do not fully capture the developmental nature of NDD pathophysiology. This review proposes a trajectory-first framework in which NDDs are interpreted as disorders of altered developmental progression. From this perspective, the key question is not only which gene, pathway, cell type, or synapse is affected, but when, where and how neurodevelopment begins to diverge. We discuss mechanisms of trajectory divergence, including altered developmental timing, cell-state and lineage disruption, selective cellular vulnerability, epigenetic and signaling dysregulation, cytoskeletal and morphogenetic abnormalities, synaptic maturation defects, excitability changes and network-level alterations. We then examine how human systems, including fetal and post-mortem atlases, iPSC-derived models, cortical organoids, assembloids, functional readouts and patient-level phenotypes, can be integrated to reconstruct developmental trajectories across biological scales. Representative NDD genes and syndromes illustrate that distinct divergence points may later converge on shared functional or clinical outcomes, including altered excitation/inhibition balance, abnormal network activity, epilepsy, language delay, intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder features or motor dysfunction. Finally, we discuss limitations and perspectives for trajectory-based stratification and biomarker discovery. Rather than acting as static diagnostic readouts, future biomarkers should aim to capture developmental state, timing, divergence, convergence, compensation and response to intervention.

records.title: Intrinsic epithelial defects and NF-κB-dependent signaling heighten viral injury in biliary atresia.
records.abstract: Targeted injury to the biliary epithelium and impaired bile flow are central mechanisms underlying childhood cholangiopathies. In biliary atresia (BA), immune-mediated cholangiocyte injury drives progressive bile duct obstruction, yet epithelial-intrinsic programs regulating injury susceptibility remain incompletely defined. Here, we modeled virus-epithelium interactions using rhesus rotavirus (RRV) infection of human liver-derived cholangiocyte organoids from normal donors (NCO) and infants with BA at diagnosis (BACO-Dx) or transplantation (BACO-Tx). Compared with NCO, BA organoids displayed baseline defects in tight junction architecture and barrier function, with prominent epithelial disruption and apoptosis following RRV exposure. Transcriptomic profiling revealed that while NCO and BACO-Dx mounted predominantly interferon-associated antiviral responses, BACO-Tx exhibited an expanded inflammatory program characterized by enrichment of NF-κB (RELA/NFKB1) regulatory network at baseline and amplified by infection. Inhibition of NF-κB signaling with the hydrogen sulfide donor GYY4137 restored organoid growth, improved tight junction organization, reduced permeability, and attenuated RRV-induced apoptosis. In the murine BA model, GYY4137 improved disease severity, preserved bile duct architecture, and protected epithelial junctional integrity while limiting cholangiocyte apoptosis. These findings identify an epithelial NF-κB-predominant program as a key determinant of intrinsic susceptibility to viral injury in BA and support targeting cholangiocyte NF-κB signaling to suppress disease progression.

records.title: Examining the Impact of Neurodevelopmental Nicotine Exposure on Cortical Excitation/Inhibition Homeostasis Markers in a Cerebral Organoid Model of Schizophrenia.
records.abstract: Schizophrenia (SCZ) is a severe neuropsychiatric disorder thought to arise from an interplay between genetic susceptibility and environmental risk factors, including prenatal nicotine exposure (PNE). Although PNE has been associated with increased risk for SCZ, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Both SCZ and PNE have independently been linked to excitation/inhibition (E/I) imbalance, suggesting that PNE may exacerbate neurodevelopmental disruptions associated with SCZ. This study employed a cerebral organoid model derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells to examine the impact of PNE on E/I-related pathways in SCZ. Organoids were chronically exposed to nicotine and analyzed using immunofluorescence and quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Results revealed disease-associated differences between SCZ and control organoids in a neural progenitor cell marker and several GABAergic, glutamatergic and cholinergic markers. Specifically, SCZ-derived organoids showed reduced SOX2 and GABAergic differentiation and synthesis markers (LHX6, GAD1/GAD67 and SST), increased select GABAergic and glutamatergic markers (GABRA1, GABRA2, GABBR2 and GRIA1), and alterations in multiple cholinergic synthesis, degradation and receptor markers. Effects of nicotine were more modest and limited to CCK, SLC6A1 and SST. These findings support a role for E/I imbalance in SCZ pathophysiology and offer insights into how early-life exposures may influence disease risk.

records.title: Teratogenic Effects and Outcomes of Congenital Oropouche Virus Infection: Current Evidence, Pathophysiological Mechanisms, and Research Priorities.
records.abstract: Oropouche virus (OROV), an Orthobunyavirus endemic to Latin America, has recently emerged as a pathogen of concern in pregnancy following reports of vertical transmission, fetal demise, congenital anomalies, and neonatal disease. The unprecedented 2023-2025 outbreaks in Latin America have expanded the geographic distribution of OROV and renewed concerns regarding its potential as an emerging human teratogen. We conducted a narrative comprehensive review of the literature focusing on epidemiology, maternal-fetal transmission, placental infection, experimental models, fetal and neonatal outcomes, and comparisons with other congenital arboviral infections. Increasing evidence supports the ability of OROV to infect the placenta, cross the maternal-fetal interface, and invade fetal tissues. Human cases have documented miscarriage, stillbirth, fetal demise, microcephaly, ventriculomegaly, cerebral atrophy, corpus callosum abnormalities, posterior fossa defects, arthrogryposis, and neonatal death following maternal infection. Viral RNA and OROV-specific antibodies have been detected in placental, fetal, and neonatal samples, providing direct evidence of congenital infection. Experimental studies using trophoblast cultures, placental organoids, neural progenitor cells, brain organoids, and animal models have confirmed placental susceptibility, vertical transmission, fetal neurotropism, and disruption of neurodevelopment. The congenital phenotype shares important similarities with congenital Zika syndrome and other neurotropic arboviral infections. OROV is newly and increasingly recognized as a vertically transmissible neurotropic arbovirus with potential teratogenic effects. Although biological plausibility is supported by converging clinical and experimental findings, prospective epidemiological studies are urgently needed to quantify risks, identify determinants of fetal injury, and define long-term outcomes among affected children.

records.title: The Tenocyte from Atom to Cell: A Critical Multiscale Synthesis Linking Collagen Chemistry, Tissue Mechanics, Cell Mechanobiology and Mathematical Modelling.
records.abstract: The tenocyte builds, maintains, senses and degrades one of the most mechanically demanding extracellular matrices in vertebrates, yet the chemical, physical, biological and mathematical descriptions of this system have developed in largely separate literatures. This review examines the tenocyte-matrix unit as a single causal system spanning eight orders of magnitude in length, organised around five transitions: from collagen chemistry to molecular mechanics; from molecule to fibril and fascicle; from tissue loading to the cellular mechanical stimulus; from stimulus to transcription; and from cellular output back to matrix composition. At each transition, we weigh competing hypotheses, identify where evidence is decisive and where it remains correlative, and state the governing equations. We integrate advances from 2021-2026, including single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlases of human tendons, the establishment of PIEZO1 as a causal regulator of tendon stiffness, and microstructurally derived constitutive models. We argue that tendon homeostasis is a closed-loop control problem, formalised as a mechanostat with an inverted-U dose-response, and that the recurrent pathologies of tendon-tendinopathy, ageing, diabetic stiffening and fibrotic healing are failures of this loop rather than of any single component. An open-source computational companion (tenocyte-virtual-cell) is introduced, and a prioritised research agenda closes the review.

records.title: Primary-Tumor Transcriptomic Signatures Associated with Circulating Tumor Cells Status in Breast Cancer: From CTC-Negative Remodeling to CTC-Associated Metastatic Programs.
records.abstract: Background/Objectives: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) play a central role in metastasis by enabling tumor dissemination through the bloodstream. However, the molecular transition from CTC-negative (CTC-) to CTC-positive (CTC+) states and their associated systemic remodeling remain poorly understood. Methods: We performed a transcriptomic comparison between CTC+, CTC-, and healthy individuals using RNA-seq data and a bioinformatics pipeline. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were subjected to functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, survival modeling, and drug perturbation prediction to delineate the molecular determinants of CTC emergence and persistence. Results: Primary tumors from CTC+ patients exhibited distinct transcriptomic profiles characterized by the upregulation of genes involved in PI3K-Akt signaling, extracellular matrix organization, and chromatin regulation (e.g., HDAC1, JUN, KLK10), alongside the downregulation of immune activation pathways, including complement, B-cell receptor (BCR), and T-cell receptor (TCR) signaling. Multi-gene survival models derived from upregulated (KLK10, MEOX2, IRS4, RND2) and downregulated (ALDH3A1, PPP2R2B, IGF1R) hub genes significantly stratified patient outcomes (HR = 1.74-2.44, p < 0.01). In contrast, primary tumors from CTC- patients displayed early systemic transcriptional alterations relative to healthy controls, with 1700+ DEGs linked to MAPK/ERK and receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) signaling pathways, suggesting pre-metastatic immune reprogramming even before CTC detection. Drug repurposing analysis identified Trichostatin A, BX-795, and Alvocidib as candidate compounds capable of reversing the CTC+ transcriptional signature. Conclusions: Rather than supporting a strictly binary view of CTC status, our findings are consistent with a transcriptional continuum of distinct yet partially overlapping primary-tumor transcriptional states associated with CTC- and CTC+ status, highlighting a molecular shift from immune suppression to epigenetic adaptation that facilitates hematogenous dissemination. The identified multi-gene prognostic panels and small-molecule candidates provide a foundation for CTC-targeted therapeutic strategies and early detection biomarkers in breast cancer.

records.title: Single-Cell Whole-Transcriptome Detection Expands the Observable RNA Space for AI Virtual-Cell Models.
records.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing has supplied cell atlases and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled virtual-cell models with scalable, gene-level descriptions of cellular state. Yet prevalent poly(A)-based counting assays capture only part of the RNA landscape. Here, "single-cell whole-transcriptome detection" denotes sequencing-based efforts to detect a broader range of RNA biotypes than conventional poly(A)-based gene counting; no assay detects or quantifies every cellular RNA species without bias. We compare RNA-capture scope, transcript-structure resolution, temporal labeling, spatial context, and additional modalities as distinct measurement dimensions. From a biosensing perspective, analytical sensitivity, transcript coverage, throughput, and assay bias determine which signals are available to computational models. We then examine cell-state representations, regulatory networks, dynamics, perturbation prediction, and foundation models. Total-RNA assays reveal additional non-coding RNAs, long-read methods inform transcript structure, and temporal assays constrain RNA kinetics. Whether these signals improve prediction beyond conventional gene-count inputs requires matched, task-specific model comparisons. We distinguish molecular observability, statistical association, predictive performance, and causal validation, which requires appropriate interventions. We propose benchmarks controlling sequencing depth, cost, model architecture, and held-out samples while testing feature ablations, out-of-distribution performance, uncertainty calibration, and experimental outcomes. Together, high-throughput poly(A)-based profiling and broader RNA measurements provide complementary cellular breadth and regulatory depth.

records.title: Virtual cells: progress and challenges from mechanistic modeling to data-driven integration.
records.abstract: Virtual cells aim to represent cellular states computationally and predict responses to genetic, chemical, environmental, temporal, and spatial conditions. For comparative purposes, this review uses state encoding (E), state transition (T), and observation decoding (D) as a conceptual abstraction spanning explicit mechanistic models, data-driven foundation and perturbation models, multimodal systems, and spatial and multiscale simulation. We examine model boundaries, data foundations, resource disclosure, out-of-distribution evaluation, causal evidence, and experimental validation. Independent benchmarks show that parameter count and training-set size do not automatically yield robust out-of-distribution generalization, while transcriptomic representations alone do not capture the full functional state of a cell. Trustworthy virtual cells will require perturbation-responsive transitions, cross-modal alignment, continuous-time dynamics, mechanistic constraints, calibrated uncertainty, independent experimental validation, and, where appropriate, closed-loop experimental feedback.

records.title: Progress of metabolomics-centric multi-omics research in medicine.
records.abstract: Metabolomics reveals molecular changes at the metabolic level during biological processes. Recent advancements, particularly through integration with other omics and artificial intelligence (AI), are advancing metabolic data analysis and multi-omics interpretation. This review introduces a "metabolomics-centric" paradigm as a conceptual framework for multi-omics integration, positioning metabolic readouts as the functional anchor for interpreting genotype-phenotype relationships. It also chronicles the evolution and medical applications of integration technologies. Our discussion first traces the field's evolution from bulk to single-cell and spatial methodologies, next surveys integration strategies to uncover mechanistic insights, and finally examines how AI-driven multimodal data integration and AI-optimized metabolomics workflows tackle persistent biological and computational challenges. Looking forward, this review identifies the AI virtual cell as a pivotal future direction for metabolomics-based multi-omics integration, calling for increased attention to its development to simulate dynamic molecular phenotypic networks within a multi-omics context.

records.title: Emerging frontiers for AI in single-cell genomics.
records.abstract: We are just over a decade into the single-cell revolution in biology, which has been coupled to the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in single-cell genomics. Most early single-cell RNA embedding models and subsequent "foundation models"-representational models pretrained on large single-cell datasets-did not gain wide traction among experimental biologists. However, as massive single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlas efforts ramp up, there is a clear rationale for exploiting AI models to interpret new datasets in the context of vast existing data resources. Meanwhile, the advent of single-cell epigenetic/multiomic assays and Perturb-seq technologies presents new opportunities for AI modeling. Here, we review AI embedding and foundation models for scRNA-seq and single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq), extensive machine-learning efforts to exploit single-cell multiome in regulatory genomics, and AI strategies to learn "virtual cell" models from Perturb-seq, ending with a description of current limitations of single-cell AI models and an outlook for future advances.

records.title: Structure-Function Relationships of Cid1 Poly(U) Polymerase: Catalysis, Substrate Recognition, Engineering, and Applications.
records.abstract: RNA 3'-end modification is an important regulatory mechanism that influences RNA processing, stability, localization, function, and degradation. Beyond its biological roles, RNA 3'-end modification has become a valuable tool in biotechnology, enabling applications in RNA labelling, sequencing, engineering and oligonucleotide synthesis. Terminal nucleotidyltransferases are key enzymes responsible for template-independent nucleotide addition to RNA molecules. Among these enzymes, Schizosaccharomyces pombe Cid1, a poly(U) polymerase, has emerged as an important model for understanding RNA-specific terminal nucleotidyltransferase activity. Structural and biochemical studies have revealed how nucleotide recognition, metal-ion-dependent catalysis, RNA positioning, and conformational dynamics regulate Cid1-mediated uridylation. Recent advances in protein engineering, molecular simulation, machine learning, and generative protein design have further expanded Cid1 functionality, generating variants with improved activity, altered substrate specificity, and potential applications in enzymatic RNA synthesis. This review summarizes the biological functions, structural characteristics, catalytic mechanisms, protein engineering strategies, and emerging biotechnological applications of Cid1, as well as the remaining challenges, highlighting its potential as a programmable platform for RNA 3'-end functionalization and enzymatic RNA oligonucleotide synthesis.

records.title: DRAGON-3D: an electron-density-aware generative model for dual-target drug molecule generation.
records.abstract: Dual-target drug molecule generation is a significant computational challenge due to the structural constraints imposed by two protein binding pockets. Existing generative models typically rely on scarce dual-target drug datasets and struggle to capture three-dimensional (3D) structural and physicochemical interactions between protein pockets and ligands, limiting generalization to new target pairs. To address these limitations, we propose DRAGON-3D, a general dual-target drug molecule generation model based on latent-space fusion of 3D electron-density representations of diverse target pairs. Our model employs a novel bi-Net β-VAE architecture and an innovative dual-pretraining strategy, enabling dual-target molecule generation using only single-target data. By integrating 3D spatial electron-density with 2D molecular topology, DRAGON-3D enhances generalization and spatial compatibility across diverse dual-target protein pairs. Comprehensive benchmarks show that DRAGON-3D is a promising framework for the generation of candidate dual-target molecules, particularly in molecular diversity, drug-likeness (QED), deployability, generalizability, and interpretability. Overall, DRAGON-3D provides an efficient, interpretable, and electron-density-informed paradigm for de novo dual-target molecular generation.

records.title: Shared α-helix chimeraffibodies enable linker-free bispecific protein design.
records.abstract: Small protein scaffolds enable precise targeting but often rely on flexible linkers that increase conformational heterogeneity and immunogenic liabilities. Here we develop Chimeraffibodies (CABs), a linker-free bispecific scaffold class that encodes interdomain geometry through seamless α-helix sharing. CABs are designed by AlphaSync, a structure-design framework that defines domain orientation through closed-form exhaustive local rigid-body superposition and ProteinMPNN-based sequence refinement. Using HER2-binding affibody and an albumin-binding domain, we generated 861CM, which preserved parental paratopes while enforcing a defined shared-helix architecture. Structural, biophysical and cellular analyses demonstrated stable assembly, cooperative target recruitment and retained affinity, with HSA binding of ∼14.3 pM and HER2 binding of 610 pM in the albumin-bound state. In vivo imaging revealed sustained tumor localization, reduced hepatic and renal background and improved organ-to-tumor contrast. CABs establish helix sharing as a geometry-encoded strategy for generating compact, homogeneous, and pharmacokinetically optimized bispecific proteins.

records.title: EquiDesign: a versatile computational framework for de novo protein sequence design.
records.abstract: Designing amino acid sequences that uniquely fold into target three-dimensional conformations defines the protein inverse folding problem, a formidable bottleneck in de novo protein design. Current computational paradigms, including deep learning-based approaches, often struggle to reconcile high sequence accuracy with structural stability, computational efficiency, and generalizability across diverse protein families. Here, we present EquiDesign, a deep learning framework that surmounts these constraints via a novel multistep Equiformer-enhanced architecture. By disentangling geometric features into invariant scalars and equivariant vectors, EquiDesign preserves the intrinsic directional topology of the protein backbone during message passing. This is achieved through spatial K-nearest neighbor graph construction and geometric attention mechanisms that hierarchically fuse multiscale contextual information, yielding a physically grounded representation of protein conformations. Extensive benchmarking demonstrates that EquiDesign achieves superior sequence recovery on standard and challenging test sets compared with state-of-the-art methods. Critically, the generated sequences exhibit exceptional structural fidelity, folding stability, and sequence diversity, as validated by comprehensive controls against training-set memorization, compositional bias, and physical energy landscapes, alongside targeted diversity sampling. These results establish EquiDesign as a robust, scalable, and generalizable inverse folding solution, driven by SE(3)-equivariant encoding and multiscale geometric attention, thus propelling de novo protein design toward unprecedented structural precision.

records.title: Building a Physically Interpretable Compressed Chemical Space via Grid-Based Optimization.
records.abstract: In recent years, deep generative models have been increasingly adopted for molecular optimization and design. In many such models, molecules are encoded into latent spaces that provide compact representations of their features. However, these latent spaces remain difficult to interpret in physical terms, and it is unclear how much structural and molecular information is retained under compression. This limitation becomes especially important when molecular behavior depends on specific three-dimensional arrangements embedded in an environmental context. Here, we introduce COMPRESS (Compression Of Molecular Physical fields into Reduced Spatial Sites), an optimization framework that represents a small molecule using a fixed number of physically parametrized spatial sites. Each site is defined by three spatial coordinates and three interaction parameters, yielding a fixed-size representation that remains directly interpretable in physical terms. To preserve molecular information, COMPRESS representations are optimized to reproduce the density, electrostatic, and van der Waals fields of the corresponding all-atom molecule on discretized three-dimensional grids. We systematically evaluate how molecular information is retained as the number of sites, K, is reduced. Our analysis covers benzene, 20 chemically diverse chemical scaffolds, benzene dimers, protein-ligand complexes, and 10,000 molecules chosen from the GEOM-Drugs data set. Across systems, field agreement deteriorates slowly at high resolution and then undergoes a rapid, pronounced transition at lower resolution. We further find that K = 25 conformers capture about 97% of the molecules from GEOM-Drugs under a loss threshold of 0.05, which we use as an indicator of fidelity. These results show that COMPRESS can provide a fixed-size, physically interpretable molecular representation, enabling compression to be evaluated directly using molecular interaction fields and resulting physical quantities. We also introduce a decoder that reconstructs all-atom structures directly from a COMPRESS representation, showing that the representation can support molecular generation in addition to field-preservation analysis. Finally, rationally modified COMPRESS representations through changes to site charge and size or the addition or removal of sites are shown to generate realistic chemical compounds upon decoding.

records.title: Programming N-linked glycan composition through de novo protein design.
records.abstract: N-linked glycans are ubiquitous post-translational modifications that mediate diverse biological processes, including cell signaling and adhesion, molecular recognition, and host-pathogen interactions. Despite their importance, N-linked glycans have largely remained beyond the reach of biomolecular design due to a lack of methods capable of jointly modeling glycans and protein structure. Here, we develop a general all-atom computational pipeline for creating de novo glycoproteins in which the amino acid sequence encodes both the location and composition of N-linked glycans. The method uses three-dimensional protein structure to tune glycan accessibility to processing enzymes in the eukaryotic secretory pathway. Systematic increases in steric restriction progressively reduced processing, shifting glycans from heterogeneous complex-type structures toward increasingly underprocessed oligomannose-type species resembling those found on many viral glycoproteins. Despite this programmed restriction, the resulting oligomannose glycans remained accessible for biological recognition, inhibiting uropathogenic Escherichia coli adhesion to human bladder cells and binding mannose-binding lectin. These results establish steric control of N-glycan processing as a genetically encodable design principle and extend computational protein design to functional glycoproteins with programmed composition.

records.title: Prospective circulating tumour DNA surveillance in patients with early high-risk hormone receptor positive, HER2-negative breast cancer in the TRAK-ER study.
records.abstract: CtDNA detection during adjuvant endocrine therapy (ET) strongly associates with recurrence in oestrogen receptor (ER) positive early breast cancer (EBC), with potential to direct switches in adjuvant treatment. TRAK-ER is a multicentre study for patients with high-risk, ER-positive, HER2-negative EBC, who undergo 3 monthly ctDNA surveillance for up to 3 years during adjuvant ET. High-risk included ≥4 involved lymph nodes; tumour >5 cm; 1-3 involved lymph nodes with additional high-risk features. Upon ctDNA detection, patients have staging scans and in the absence of radiological recurrence, are randomised to receive palbociclib plus fulvestrant or standard ET. ctDNA analysis was performed using a tumour informed assay (Labcorp). We report a protocol-specified analysis of ctDNA detection during surveillance, and results of contemporaneous radiological recurrence. 1133 patients were registered by September 2025, 928 had panels designed (design failed in 16.1% (178/1106), and 912 started ctDNA surveillance including results from 5810 tests (median 7 per patient). ctDNA detection rate was 5.0% (45/897) in the first test, and 1.3% (66/4913) in subsequent tests (P<0.001). Patient level detection rate was 12.0% (109/912), with 1.1% (10/912) of patients having a clinical recurrence without prior ctDNA detection. Detection positively associated with nodal burden (P<0.001) and grade (P=0.04) and negatively associated with increasing time from surgery (P=0.01). Estimated cumulative ctDNA detection rate at 5 years post-surgery was 23.7% (95%CI 14.5-31.9%). In patients with ctDNA detected on the first test, 65.9% (29/44) had radiological recurrence compared to 26.6% (17/64) in patients first detected on subsequent tests (P<0.001). Results from TRAK-ER inform implementation of ctDNA surveillance in ER-positive EBC, including molecular relapse rates, factors associating with ctDNA detection and contemporaneous radiological recurrence. Ultrasensitive assays detecting ctDNA at low levels, are required to robustly identify patients prior to clinical recurrence. TRAK-ER is ongoing to assess the impact of treatment after molecular relapse detection.

records.title: PARP Inhibitors in the Management of Ovarian Cancer: ASCO Living Guideline, Version 2026.1.0.
records.abstract: This living guideline provides recommendations on the use of poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPis) in the management of epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC). An Expert Panel developed recommendations based on a systematic review of randomized controlled trials, and cohort studies evaluating homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) testing and PARPi efficacy and safety. The updated evidence base comprises 79 publications, including 18 studies evaluating 13 homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) assays and 31 pivotal trials assessing PARPi efficacy and safety. Frontline trials demonstrated progression-free survival benefits. However, later-line treatment and recurrent maintenance trials reported potential overall survival disadvantages. All patients with newly diagnosed advanced EOC should undergo genetic testing, and HRD tumor testing if BRCA-negative, using FDA-approved or prospectively validated companion diagnostic assays. In advanced EOC, PARPi maintenance should be prioritized for the first clinical remission. Frontline PARPi monotherapy maintenance should be offered after platinum-based chemotherapy response to patients with germline or somatic BRCA1/2 mutations or HRD-positive disease. Olaparib plus bevacizumab maintenance may be offered to patients responding to first-line platinum-based chemotherapy plus bevacizumab who have BRCA1/2 mutations or HRD-positive disease. PARPi maintenance therapy is not recommended for patients with non-BRCAmut HRD-negative tumors or early-stage EOC. In the recurrent setting, PARPi maintenance should be restricted primarily to PARPi-naïve patients with BRCA1/2 mutations responding to second-line or greater platinum-based chemotherapy. Monotherapy PARPi should not be offered for the treatment of recurrent EOC outside clinical trials. Furthermore, PARPi are not recommended for use in combination with chemotherapy, other targeted agents, or immune-oncology agents outside a clinical trial. Clinicians should monitor for serious adverse events, including myelodysplastic syndrome, acute myeloid leukemia, and pulmonary complications.

records.title: Deep-Learning-Assisted Integrated Microfluidic Platform for Automated Analysis of EV RNA Mutations.
records.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) carry key genetic biomarkers, such as somatic mutations, making them valuable targets for non-invasive cancer diagnostics. However, standard workflows that isolate EVs and detect low-abundance mutations typically require multi-step manual operations, leading to sample loss and potential cross-contamination. Here, we present an integrated microfluidic platform combined with a deep learning algorithm for the continuous processing and automated droplet analysis of EV-derived RNA mutations. The microfluidic chip integrates magnetic bead-based EV capture, online lysis, droplet generation, and arrayed RT-droplet digital PCR (RT-ddPCR) on a single device. To streamline signal readout, a deep learning framework based on Cellpose and K-means clustering was implemented to process individual fluorescence images, enabling droplet detection, background removal, gray-scale intensity extraction, and automatic positive/negative droplet classification. The system showed a linear response across a wide range of original-sample inputs (R2 = 0.9950). The platform was evaluated using EV samples derived from three cancer cell lines (NCI-H1975, SK-LU-1, and HepG2) and the detection of EGFR L858R and KRAS mutations were achieved. By coupling continuous sample processing with automated image interpretation, this platform offers a practical reference for integrated EV nucleic acid analysis for liquid-biopsy applications.

records.title: Preoperative Assessment of Circulating Extracellular Vesicles as a Potential Biomarker for Melanoma.
records.abstract: Circulating extracellular vesicle (EV)-associated particle profiles may differ between patients with melanoma and those with benign lesions. Preoperative citrated whole blood from 77 patients with clinically suspicious lesions was assessed by direct fluorescence-based flow cytometry; histopathology identified 20 CMM cases (12 primary and 8 metastatic) and 57 benign-lesion controls. The reported total particle concentration was higher in CMM than controls (3299.86 ± 456.61 vs. 2873.40 ± 427.74 events/µL). CD45+, PD-L1+, and CD45+/PD-L1+ populations were also increased. CD45+/VISTA+ particles were higher in the reduced subset of 9 CMM cases and 48 controls. These exploratory observations require analytical validation and independent clinical confirmation before diagnostic or prognostic utility can be established.

records.title: Circulating Tumour Cell GALNT13 Expression Is Associated with Prognosis and Treatment Response in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
records.abstract: Reliable circulating biomarkers for prognosis and treatment monitoring in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain limited. Liquid biopsy offers a minimally invasive approach to identify clinically informative tumour-derived markers. Given the emerging role of GalNAc-transferases in cancer biology, we evaluated GALNT13 expression in peripheral blood as a potential biomarker for prognosis and disease monitoring in lung cancer patients. Sensitive molecular assays (nested and digital RT-PCR) were developed to detect GALNT13 mRNA in circulating tumour cells (CTCs). These methods were applied to peripheral blood samples from non-small cell lung cancer patients to assess prognostic value and enable longitudinal monitoring. A cohort of 143 NSCLC patients was analysed, of whom 60% were GALNT13-positive in peripheral blood at baseline. During a five-year follow-up, GALNT13 positivity was significantly associated with reduced overall survival. In several patients, increases in GALNT13 levels preceded radiologic evidence of disease progression. GALNT13 expression in CTCs emerges as a promising biomarker for prognosis and treatment monitoring in NSCLC. Prospective studies in larger cohorts are warranted to validate its clinical utility.

records.title: Serum Proteomic Profiling by SomaScan Aptamer Array Identifies Candidate Predictive and Monitoring Biomarkers of Distant Recurrence in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
records.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) lacks a blood-based biomarker for predicting or monitoring distant recurrence. We profiled 39 serum samples from 38 women (10 healthy controls; 12 non-recurrent [NR]; eight diagnosis-timepoint samples from patients who later recurred [DR-DIG]; nine recurrence-timepoint samples [DR-REC]) using the SomaScan v5.0 aptamer platform). Public tumor-tissue transcriptomic cohorts were used for supportive and exploratory analyses. No protein reached a false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.05 for NR vs. DR-DIG; granzyme A (GZMA) and endoplasmic reticulum aminopeptidase 1 (ERAP1) showed the strongest nominal signals. For DR-DIG vs. DR-REC, 38 aptamers (37 proteins) reached FDR < 0.05, enriched for RNA-binding and nuclear-envelope proteins; this signature was retained in leave-one-out and storage-adjusted analyses. Higher GZMA mRNA was associated with longer recurrence-free survival in two independent cohorts (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.795, p = 0.018; HR = 0.186, p = 0.0057). Monitor genes showed near-chance concordance with metastatic tissue, and the source of the signature could not be resolved. An exploratory four-gene elastic-net panel reached a concordance index of 0.613 internally but 0.559 externally. GZMA is a candidate serum biomarker of TNBC recurrence risk, and the monitor signature is a preliminary observation. Both require protein-level validation in independent, prospectively collected serum cohorts.
